correctness.rationale: The graph is defined explicitly and an isomorphism to \(GP(10,3)\) is verified. All 113,192 faces (including empty) are enumerated. A complete staged face-poset pairing gives 56,567 ordinary matched pairs and critical cells one critical zero-cell, eight five-cells and forty-eight six-cells. Full Hasse orientation is acyclic by exact topological sort of 680,370 incidences. Signed integral gradient-path elimination computes the full 8-by-48 degree matrix: its columns lie in the primitive lattice generated by \(e_0-e_1\), \(e_3\) and \(e_6-e_7\), and columns 2,9,36 equal those generators. The resulting integer Smith factors are 1,1,1. The 5-skeleton is a wedge of eight 5-spheres, whose \(\pi_5\) is \(\mathbb Z^8\), so the integral degree matrix classifies all 6-cell attachments. Three unit attachments cancel, leaving five 5-spheres and forty-five 6-spheres. The final exact verifier is included and executable; finite numerical data alone are not treated as proof of a family statement.

value.rationale: The ordinary matching complex of the canonical 20-vertex Desargues (middle-level) graph is naturally motivated by graph matching topology. Prior exact mod-two homology concentrated in two adjacent dimensions did not settle torsion, higher attaching maps, or the homotopy type. A primitive integral Morse boundary of rank three settles these questions in a substantive finite case with an explicit reproducible homotopy model, not a routine rank recomputation. The claim is restricted to the smallest precise natural object under examination; no general theorem is falsely promised.
